title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics + schema mapping + tool message formatting
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Align Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling with OpenAI's tool_choice semantics and parameter schema mapping, and standardize tool message formatting. This PR unblocks customers migrating from OpenAI-style tool calling and fixes edge cases observed in streaming+toolcall flows.

Changes in scope: mapping Redwood tool descriptors to OpenAI-style 'parameters' schema, clarifying tool_choice (assistant selects a tool by name vs. direct tool call) behavior, adding deterministic message formatting rules for tool outputs (role tagging, content/json shape), improving streaming stability during tool handoff, and extensive tests + docs.

Checklist: [x] Implement schema mapping layer to emit OpenAI-compatible 'parameters' objects; [x] Implement tool_choice handling in openai_compat router; [x] Normalize tool result messages to include "role": "tool" and structured content field when JSON is returned; [x] Ensure streaming paths do not duplicate messages during tool handoff; [x] Add unit and integration tests; [x] Update docs and migration guide; [x] Add backwards-compatible toggle (openai_compat.tool_choice_v1) for rollout.

Compatibility notes: The new mapping is opt-in via config flag openai_compat.tool_choice_v2=false->true. When enabled, Redwood will map internal tool schemas to OpenAI-style JSON Schema in the tools list returned to callers, and will respect 'tool_choice' messages coming from models by emitting a synthetic assistant message of the form {"name": "<tool>", "type": "tool_choice"} followed by the tool invocation. We deliberately keep a compatibility flag because some existing integrations rely on the previous flattened tool message format.

Testing: Added unit tests for schema translation, end-to-end tests that exercise streaming + tool handoff, and a small canary on staging for traffic patterns that previously caused doubled messages. CI initially failed on lint due to formatting in openai_compat/formatters.py; fixed in second commit.

Docs & migration: docs/openai_compat.md contains a migration section with examples comparing old vs. new tool messages and recommended server-side handling. Also added a compatibility note in redwood-docs site and an example in redwood-examples/openai_tool_choice_demo.py.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-8923 (tool calling stability), PM-428 (OpenAI-compat feature spec), SUP-342 (customer migration request).
